summary: Role resolution fails after Okta group id type change; ModelObservability API returns 403 for newly provisioned users
description: Summary: Since 2026-03-09 ~03:00 UTC a subset of newly provisioned users are getting 403 when calling the ModelObservability API. Initial triage shows users exist in OKTA and have expected groups, but the RBAC role lookup in auth-service fails because group identifiers in the incoming auth claim are integers instead of strings after a recent Okta mapping change. Impact: Affected SREs and ML engineers cannot access model observability dashboards or runbook actions; blocking incident response in us-east for customer-impacting alerts.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create or modify an Okta user with group assignment via provisioning (SCIM).
2) Wait for scim-sync job to run (0-5m).
3) Login to console and call /v1/model-observability/metrics (or open dashboard).
4) Observe 403 and no role in auth-service logs for the user.
Expected: role lookup succeeds and 200 returned. Actual: 403 denied due to missing role mapping.
investigation_notes:
Timeline: change window 2026-03-08 22:00 UTC when Okta admin updated group import mapping to emit numeric IDs (Okta API update). Hypothesis: identity-proxy and scim-sync historically normalized group ids to strings; the new mapping produced integers and our role index uses string keys -> lookup misses.
Findings:
- scim-sync stored groups in DB as strings when coming from canonical SCIM paths, but identity-proxy forwards token claims verbatim.
- auth-service role lookup code compares claim group IDs with role-index map (string keys). No type coercion.
- Reproduced locally by forging token with numeric group values; role lookup returns empty.
- Not all users affected: only those provisioned after Okta mapping change (group ids numeric). Older tokens remain as strings and continue to work.
Evidence: logs above and successful reproduction in staging by creating token with numeric groups.
Mitigation attempted: temporary canary: identity-proxy will coerce numeric claim.groups to strings on ingress; deployed to canary cluster (canary-2) 2026-03-11 18:30 UTC.
comments: 2026-03-10 04:05 - Priya Kapoor (Support): Reported initial customer-facing impact after SRE oncall noted missing access for 3 engineers. Attached sample decoded token and stack trace.

2026-03-10 06:12 - Diego Morales (Auth): Reproduced locally. Hypothesis: type mismatch between Okta claim payload and our role-index typing. Filed quick PR to normalize types in identity-proxy. Linking PR to this ticket.
2026-03-11 19:05 - Samir Patel (SRE): Canary deploy applied to canary-2. Observed two previously-401/403 requests now succeed. Monitoring for 24h to confirm no regressions.

2026-03-12 09:20 - Priya Kapoor (Support): Customer-facing note drafted: "We identified a token group id encoding mismatch caused by an Okta mapping update. A temporary fix has been deployed to canary and will be rolled to prod after validation. Apologize for the disruption."
resolution: Hotfix: identity-proxy change (PR #498) coerces all group ids in the token claim to strings on ingress and emits a metric for any non-string group values. Auth-service change (PR #1257) added defensive coercion for role lookup as backup. Canary results: successful requests for previously affected users on canary-2. Rollout plan: staged rollout to prod us-east 2026-03-12 15:00 UTC with monitoring and immediate rollback on elevated error rates. Root cause: Okta mapping change that started emitting numeric group ids; our code assumed string typed ids.
follow_up:
1) Add schema validation on identity-proxy (block incoming tokens with unexpected types and alert).
2) Create automated unit test in auth-service for claim type coercion.
3) Ask IAM team to revert or document Okta mapping change and add approver workflow for mapping modifications.
4) Postmortem to be authored in Confluence and linked here after incident closure.
Assigned to: Diego Morales (follow-up engineering items) and Priya Kapoor (postmortem coordination).
